read.thesis: Chevron's supply-side signals are disciplined: Permian capex to below $3.5B (25% lower per boe) and full-year capex at the low end of $18-19B, though record output and a 2.67 GW Microsoft power PPA add new growth vectors.

triggers.label: Permian capex below $3.5B, 25% better per boe
triggers.quote: Our capital is now, we expect it to be below $3.5 billion this year. So that's a 25% improvement in capital efficiency.

triggers.label: Full-year capex at low end of $18-19B
triggers.quote: We now expect to finish the year at the lower end of our guidance range of $18 billion to $19 billion.

triggers.label: 2.67 GW Microsoft behind-the-meter PPA
triggers.quote: We recently signed a 20-year take-or-pay power purchase agreement with Microsoft for 2.67 gigawatts of firm behind-the-meter capacity

triggers.label: Refinery crude utilisation 97%
triggers.quote: representing a 97% crude unit utilization rate during the second quarter

triggers.label: Middle distillate cracks widening into Q3
triggers.quote: So I think we're going to see some upward pressure on product pricing here into the third quarter

guidance.quote: We now expect to finish the year at the lower end of our guidance range of $18 billion to $19 billion.
Our capital is now, we expect it to be below $3.5 billion this year.
including annual production growth of 2% to 3%, adjusted free cash flow growth averaging greater than 10% per year

We expect that by early 2027, that will be fully recovered.
